about.title: About
about.description: Four things we will not do to your site, and four we will. Fixed scope, fixed price, no mandatory retainer, and the code is yours the day it ships.
about.heading: Four things we will not do. Four we will.
about.intro: No hedging, no small print. If any of this stops being true you will be the first to notice, which is rather the point of writing it down.

templates.note: Someone else's answer to someone else's problem, and every hour after installing it goes on bending it toward yours.

builders.note: Nested containers that mean nothing to a screen reader, a search engine, or the next developer who opens the file.

retainers.note: A site should not need a subscription to stay upright. If it does, something was built wrong. Ongoing marketing or content work, if you want it, is a separate and optional service.

surprises.note: A change halfway through is a conversation. You will never find out what it cost by reading a bill.

scope.note: Every page and every feature written down before anything is built — including what is explicitly not included.

price.note: Priced with the scope, and it does not move underneath you.

code.note: The repository is yours the day it ships. Another developer can pick it up without asking us for anything.

accounts.note: Domain, hosting and analytics in your name. Nothing is held hostage by being registered under ours.

about.deeperBody: Every step, what we need from you at each one, and roughly how long it takes.

approach.title: How we work
approach.description: The whole process, written down: every step of a JalimX project, what we need from you at each one, how long it takes, and what every site gets regardless of budget.
approach.body: Most studios will tell you it depends. Here is the sequence instead — what we need from you at each step, roughly how long each one takes, and what happens when you want to change something halfway through.

telemetry.label: This page, in your browser
telemetry.note: Read from your browser's Performance API as this page loaded. Not our numbers — yours. Reload and watch them settle.

approach.processIntro: Five steps. The only one with a variable length is the build, and the scope document tells you which end of the range you are at before you pay anything.
approach.processTerms: Half at scope, half at launch. Two review rounds included.

call.name: The call
call.body: A conversation, not a pitch. What the site has to do, who it is for, and what is not working now. If we are not the right people for it, you will hear that on this call rather than in week three.
call.need: Forty-five minutes, and honesty about the budget.

scope.name: The scope
scope.body: A written document: every page, every feature, what is explicitly not included, and one fixed price. You can hand it to another studio and get a comparable quote — that is rather the point of writing it down.
scope.need: Your content, or a decision that we write it.

build.name: The build
build.body: You get a link on the first day and it updates as we go. There is no reveal at the end. If something is wrong, it is wrong while it is still cheap to change.
build.need: Answers within a day or two, from one person.

review.name: Your review
review.body: You go through the whole thing and write one list. We work through the list. Two rounds are included in the price, and we have not yet needed a third.
review.need: One list, not five separate emails.

live.name: Live
live.body: Domain, certificate, redirects from whatever was there before, and a walkthrough of your dashboard — recorded, so you can watch it again in six months when you have forgotten.
live.need: Access to the domain, or we buy it in your name.

approach.standardIntro: Not a package tier. These are not negotiable down, because a site without them costs you more later than it saved you now.

standard.a: Fast on a phone on a bad connection — not just on a laptop on office wifi.
standard.b: Usable with a keyboard, and readable by a screen reader.
standard.c: Findable: real markup, real metadata, a real sitemap.
standard.d: Editable by you, from a dashboard built for your site rather than a generic admin panel.
standard.e: In both languages, if your customers are in both.
standard.f: Still standing in two years without a monthly retainer to keep it upright.

a.title: The content
a.body: Text, prices, images and translations, editable from a dashboard built for your site rather than a generic admin panel.

b.title: The code
b.body: The repository is yours. If we stop working together another developer picks it up — it is ordinary code in a framework you can hire for, not a proprietary system.

c.title: The domain and the accounts
c.body: Registered in your name, hosted under your account. Nothing is held hostage by being registered under ours.

approach.limitsIntro: Saying this out loud saves us both a call.

limits.a: Customise a WordPress or Shopify theme. If a theme is the right answer, you do not need us.
limits.b: Patch an existing page-builder site. Working inside one costs more than starting over, and the result is still built on the thing that caused the problem.
limits.c: Start without someone who can decide. We need one person on your side who can answer questions and sign things off. No amount of planning rescues a project that cannot get an answer.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.heading: What happens to what you send us.
privacy.intro: Short, because there is little to say. The site has a contact form and nothing else that collects anything. Here is what it does with the form.

who.heading: Who we are
who.body: JalimX is a web development studio based in Marrakech, Morocco. We decide why and how the information on this page is used. To ask about it, write to

collect.heading: What we collect
collect.body: Only what you type into the contact form, and what comes with it:
items: Your name, email address and phone number (a WhatsApp number, so we can continue the conversation there).
Your company, the kind of work you need and your budget, if you chose to fill those in.
Your message, and the language of the page you wrote from.
Your IP address, kept to spot abuse of the form. It is never shown on the site and is not used to identify you.

why.heading: Why we use it
why.body: To answer you and, if you want one, prepare a written scope and price. We also use the IP address and a spam check to keep the form free of automated messages. We do not use it for advertising, we do not sell it, and there is no newsletter.

share.heading: Who else handles it
share.body: Services that run the site for us, and nothing beyond them:
items: Vercel hosts the website, and Railway and Neon run the server and database where enquiries are stored.
Cloudflare provides the spam check (Turnstile) that runs in your browser on the contact page.
An email provider delivers our replies and the notice that a message arrived.
share.after: Some of these providers process data outside Morocco and the European Union. If you move to WhatsApp or email, those services' own terms apply to what you send there.

keep.heading: How long we keep it
keep.body: For as long as it takes to answer you and, if it becomes a project, for the project and the records it requires. An enquiry that goes nowhere is deleted when you ask.

cookies.heading: Cookies and tracking
cookies.body: The site sets no cookies, has no analytics and no advertising trackers, and does not follow you to other sites. The spam check may use short-lived storage in your browser to tell a visitor from a script.

rights.heading: Your rights
rights.body: You can ask what we hold about you, have it corrected, or have it deleted, and you can object to its use. This applies under Moroccan law 09-08 and, if you are in the European Union, under the GDPR. Write to the address above and we will answer within 30 days. You can also complain to the Moroccan data protection authority (CNDP) or to the authority in your own country.

changes.heading: Changes
changes.body: If the site starts collecting anything new, this page is updated first and the date at the top changes.

tourism.heading: Websites for tour operators, desert camps and villas in Morocco.
tourism.intro: Built so guests book with you directly: in their language, on their phone, with an answer before they leave. Every client on this page now takes bookings through their own site.

problems.note: When the only way to book is a marketplace, it takes its share of every room and every tour, and keeps the guest's details.
Guests arrive from France, Spain, Britain and the Gulf. A site that speaks to one of them loses the others at the first page.

problems.term: No answer at eleven at night.
problems.note: A guest with one question before booking will not wait until morning. They book the camp next door.
A site where every tour sits on one page cannot rank for any of them.

build.note: Tours, rooms, tents, day passes and prices, each on its own page, changed from your own dashboard.
A booking request that reaches you straight away, or a full booking system with availability, depending on how you work.
Our clients' sites run in two, three or four languages, each written properly, not machine-translated on the fly.
One tap from any page to a conversation with you, so the question gets answered before they look elsewhere.
Most guests plan on a phone, often on a weak connection. The site is built for that first, not shrunk down from a laptop.
Every tour and every room has its own address, title and description, with the structured data Google reads.

tourism.proofNote: Each of these clients started taking bookings through their own website.
how: A short call about the business: who books, what they ask, where bookings are lost today.
A written scope with a fixed price, including what is not included. Nothing starts before you accept it.
The site, the dashboard and the code are yours the day it goes live.
tourism.howLink: The whole process, step by step

faq.q: Can I change tours, rooms and prices myself?
faq.a: Yes. Every site comes with its own dashboard. Changing a price, adding a tour or swapping photos does not need us.

faq.q: Do I keep my Booking.com and Airbnb listings?
faq.a: Yes. The website adds a direct channel next to them, so the guests who find you can book without a commission. We can also set those listings up, as we did for Villa Elk.

faq.q: Which languages can the site have?
faq.a: As many as your guests need. Our clients' sites run in two, three or four languages.

faq.q: How do guests reach me?
faq.a: Through a booking request or booking form on the site, and through WhatsApp from any page if you use it.

faq.q: Will the site appear on Google?
faq.a: Every page is built to be indexed: its own title and description, structured data, and fast loading on a phone. Rankings also depend on content and links built over time, so we do not promise positions.

faq.q: What does it cost, and how long does it take?
faq.a: It depends on the project. After a short call you receive a written scope with a fixed price, and you pay nothing until you accept it.

faq.q: Who owns the website?
faq.a: You do. The code, the domain and the accounts are in your name from the day the site goes live.

web-development.for: Businesses whose website has to do a job: take a booking, answer the question a customer asks before buying, or replace a spreadsheet and a phone. Most of our clients are in tourism and hospitality.

faq.q: Which technology do you use?
faq.a: Next.js for the website and Laravel for the dashboard and the data. Both are widely used, so any competent developer can work on the code after us.

faq.q: Can I change the content myself?
faq.a: Yes. Every site comes with its own dashboard for the content, the prices and the photos.

faq.q: Is the site built for Google?
faq.a: Yes: titles, descriptions, structured data, sitemaps and speed are part of the build. Rankings also depend on content and links over time, so we do not promise positions.

faq.q: What does it cost?
faq.a: It depends on the project. After a short call you receive a written scope with a fixed price, and you pay nothing until you accept it.

includes.term: A logo system, not a single logo.
includes.note: Versions for every place it has to work: the website, a profile picture, a booking platform, a printed card.
The typefaces and the palette that go with the logo, chosen to stay readable on a phone and on paper.
The rules that keep it consistent, so the identity survives the next person who touches it.
Vector files and ready exports, delivered with the guide.
On the website and on the profiles that sell, as we did for Villa Elk: Booking.com, Airbnb, Google, Instagram and Facebook.

brand-identity.for: A new business that has nothing yet, or one whose logo looks different on every platform. For a villa or a camp, the identity is what a guest recognises from one listing to the next.

faq.q: What do I receive?
faq.a: The logo system in vector files and ready exports, the typefaces and colours, and a written guide to using them.

faq.q: Can the identity be applied to my listings and social accounts?
faq.a: Yes. For Villa Elk we created the logo and set it up across Booking.com, Airbnb, Google, Instagram and Facebook, together with the website.

faq.q: What does it cost?
faq.a: It depends on the project. After a short call you receive a written scope with a fixed price.

includes.note: What to publish, when, and why, built around the seasons and offers of the business.
What to film and photograph, so what is captured on site is usable instead of random.
Written for the platform they run on and the guest they are talking to, in the guest's language.
Reusable formats for an offer, a season or an event, so every post does not start from nothing.
Profiles created or cleaned up, with the identity applied, as we did for Villa Elk's Instagram and Facebook.

content-social.for: Hospitality and tourism businesses that know guests choose on Instagram before they ever open a website, and want posts that sound like the business rather than like everyone else.

faq.q: Is content work tied to a website project?
faq.a: No. It is a separate and optional service. It works best alongside a site we built, but it does not require one.

faq.q: Which platforms do you work on?
faq.a: Instagram and Facebook first, because that is where hospitality guests look before they book.

faq.q: What does it cost?
faq.a: It depends on what the business needs. After a short call you receive a written scope with a fixed price.

includes.note: Indexing, canonical addresses, sitemaps, structured data and speed, done as part of the site rather than bolted on afterwards.
Each tour, room or service on its own page, written around what guests actually type.
Each language version tagged so search engines show the right one to the right visitor.

includes.term: Local search and Google Business Profile.
includes.note: The profile set up and kept consistent with the website, so the business shows on maps and local results.
Pages set up for Google, Bing and AI answer engines, as on the Villa Elk site.
Search Console and analytics, so you can tell whether any of it worked.

seo-growth.for: Businesses that want guests to find them on Google instead of only on booking platforms, and that would rather see the numbers than take our word for it.

faq.q: Can you guarantee the first position on Google?
faq.a: No, and nobody honestly can. Rankings depend on competition, content and links. What we commit to is the work, and the numbers that show what changed.

faq.q: Do I need a new website for SEO?
faq.a: Not always, but a site built for search from the start makes the work far more effective. Every site we build includes the technical part.

faq.q: What does it cost?
faq.a: It depends on the business and the market. After a short call you receive a written scope with a fixed price.
